title: DirectionConfirmation
description:
The combination of independent latency runs of one configuration
(`credential-eval perf confirm`). A deterministic function of the artifacts:
the order they are given in does not matter.

config_hash.description: The configuration digest every run shares.

results.description: One entry per workload and shape, sorted.

runs.description: The runs, sorted by artifact digest.

same_cpu_model.description:
Whether every run recorded the same CPU model; absent when a run did
not record one. Directions from different models are less comparable.

subjects.description: The subjects every run shares, sorted by id.

Confirmation.description: Whether a direction held across independent runs of one configuration.

oneOf.description: Every run reported `faster`.
Every run reported `slower`.

The runs disagree, or only some of them reported a direction. A
direction seen once is not a result.

Every run was `indistinguishable`. This is "no evidence", not "no
effect": the measurement could not resolve a difference.

ConfirmedResult.description: The directions of one workload and shape across the runs.

directions.description: The direction each run reported, in the order of `runs`.

Direction.description: Which way the candidate moved relative to the baseline.

oneOf.description:
The candidate is faster by more than the A/A noise band, in both the
median and the minimum.

The candidate is slower by more than the A/A noise band, in both the
median and the minimum.
Within the A/A noise band, or the median and the minimum disagree.

RunReference.description: One independent run that a confirmation was drawn from.

artifact_digest.description: SHA-256 of the run's canonical artifact, timings included.

cpu_model_digest.description: The run's CPU model, when it recorded one.

ScanShape.description: Whether the scanner receives each workload whole or in chunks.

oneOf.description: One invocation over the whole input.

One invocation per chunk of at most `chunk_bytes`, split at line
boundaries; a sample is the sum over the chunks.

SubjectIdentity.description: Identity of one subject (scanner build) in a run.

executable_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the executable, for external-process subjects.

invocation_digest.description:
Digest of how the executable is invoked: arguments, input delivery and
the exit codes that count as a scan (the subject's activation and
options; never the executable path). Recorded from revision v1.1 of the
artifact so a subject's measurement can be matched without the pair's
whole `config_hash` (ADR 0010). Absent in older artifacts, whose
subjects are then only reusable as part of their unchanged pair.

revision.description: Source revision, when built from a Git commit.

role.description:
The arm this subject measured in a pairwise run. Absent for
allocation, where the results name their subjects.

SubjectRole.description: The arm of a pairwise run a subject occupied.

oneOf.description: The build every direction is relative to (arm A and its A/A control).
The build under test (arm B).

WorkloadId.description:
A generated synthetic workload. The generator for each id is deterministic
and lives in `credential-eval-perf`; its output is identified by digest.

oneOf.description: Ordinary text with one non-ASCII character at the end.
Non-ASCII text on every line.
Ordinary text with one invisible (zero-width) character.
Invisible characters throughout.

Assignment lines whose value is also a standalone token shape, so more
than one detector claims the same range.

Secret-bearing lines with invisible characters inside the value, so
every reported range crosses a normalization seam.
The same short log line, repeated.
A few very long single-line assignments.

Assignment lines, densely, so a bounded scanner exhausts its budget
early in the input.
32-character alphanumeric values under one key.
Five keys and five value shapes.
Cloud secret-manager references and placeholders.
One `otpauth://` URI per line.
One `otpauth://` URI inside about 74 KB of ordinary log text.
One synthetic storage connection string.
100 storage connection strings, one per line.
One segment that repeats the same account-key field 100 times.
Ordinary log lines with no connection string.
Tokens on separate lines, none overlapping.
As `overlap-disjoint`, with one overlapping pair in the middle.
Every token overlaps exactly one other.
Every token overlaps its neighbours.
